# GST Bill Reconciliation — mobile client (Flutter)

Mirrors the web app's flow: capture or pick a bill photo, drag four corner
handles onto it (no automatic edge detection, matching the manual-crop
decision made for the web app), pick a rotation, send it to the backend for
perspective correction, extract with Gemini, review/edit, save, then browse
purchases and export/share the Excel workbook.

This project was hand-written without the Flutter SDK available in the
build environment, so `android/` and `ios/` native project folders are
**not included** — they're generated by the Flutter tooling itself and
version-pinned to whatever Flutter/Gradle/Xcode toolchain you have locally.
`flutter analyze` / `flutter pub get` were not run here either. You'll need
to do the one-time scaffolding step below before this builds.

## One-time setup

```bash
cd mobile
flutter create .              # generates android/, ios/, and other platform folders
                               # in place — it will not overwrite lib/ or pubspec.yaml's
                               # dependencies, but review its diff before committing
flutter pub get
```

Then add camera/photo-library usage descriptions to
`ios/Runner/Info.plist` (required by iOS — `image_picker` will crash on
first use without these, and `flutter create` doesn't add them for you):

```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>Used to photograph purchase bills for extraction.</string>
<key>NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription</key>
<string>Used to pick an existing bill photo from your library.</string>
```

Android needs no manual manifest edits — `image_picker` merges its own
required permissions into `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
automatically.

## Run

```bash
flutter run
```

On first launch, expand "Server address" on the login screen and set the
API base URL:

- Android emulator: `http://10.0.2.2:8000` (default already set)
- Physical device on the same Wi-Fi as your backend: `http://<your-computer's-LAN-IP>:8000`
- iOS simulator: `http://127.0.0.1:8000` works directly

The backend must already be running (see `../backend/README.md`) and
reachable from wherever the app runs.

## Structure

- `lib/models.dart` — Dart mirrors of the backend's Pydantic schemas.
- `lib/api_client.dart` — REST client; holds the JWT and base URL in
  `SharedPreferences`.
- `lib/widgets/crop_canvas.dart` — the draggable four-corner crop overlay.
- `lib/screens/` — login/signup, capture+crop+extract, review/edit/save,
  purchases list + Excel export (shared via the OS share sheet, since a
  mobile app can't trigger a browser-style file download).

Template-based fast-path extraction and the vendor management screen
(build order steps 5-6) aren't implemented here either, matching the
backend's current scope.
